title: Determination of four arsenic species in environmental water samples by liquid chromatography- inductively coupled plasma - tandem mass spectrometry
author: Stetson, Lawrence, et al.

steps.title: Collect and preserve water samples
steps.instruction: Filter each surface‑water or groundwater sample in the field through a 0.45 µm filter directly into a 10 mL opaque polyethylene bottle that already contains 100 µL of 250 mM EDTA (giving a final preservative concentration of 2.5 mM). Fill the bottle to the shoulder, cap, and store at 4 °C ± 2 °C until analysis.

steps.title: Add field spike (if required)
steps.instruction: For field‑spike bottles, add either 100 µL or 500 µL of a 1 000 µg L⁻¹ solution containing As(III), As(V), DMA, and MMA using a digital pipet, then weigh the bottle. Calculate the sample volume by subtracting the mean empty‑bottle weight (average of five bottles, variability < 1 %). If the spike volume exceeds 2 % of the total sample volume, correct the measured concentration for dilution. The resulting spike concentrations are approximately 10 µg L⁻¹ or 50 µg L⁻¹ for each arsenic species.

steps.title: Prepare laboratory aliquots
steps.instruction: Transfer an aliquot of each filtered sample, calibration standard, or blank into a 1 mL LC vial and spike with germanium to achieve a final concentration of 20 µg L⁻¹ Ge to eliminate the water dip on the Ge chromatogram.

steps.title: Prepare calibration and QC standards
steps.instruction: At the start of each analytical batch, prepare a calibration series and fit a linear inverse‑weighted (1/x) regression; the correlation coefficient must be ≥ 0.999. Immediately after calibration run an internal calibration verification (ICV) at 20 µg L⁻¹; its measured value must be within ± 20 % of the expected concentration. Then prepare a continuing calibration verification (CCV) at either 0.5 µg L⁻¹ or 5 µg L⁻¹ and a reagent blank; run these after the ICV, at the end of the batch, and after every ten sample injections. Bracketing calibration checks must be within ± 15 % of expected and blanks within ± the detection limit. Finally, run a limit‑of‑quantitation (LOQ) standard at 0.1 µg L⁻¹ after the calibration and again at the end of the run; its measured value must be within ± 50 % of the expected concentration.

steps.title: Set up LC‑ICP‑MS/MS system
steps.instruction: Install a Hamilton PRP‑X100 anion‑exchange column and deliver the optimized nitrate/phosphate mobile phase (concentrations and pH previously optimized for maximum As(III)–DMA resolution). Set the total analysis time to approximately 15 min per injection. Connect the LC outlet to an inductively coupled plasma tandem mass spectrometer (ICP‑QQQ) configured for arsenic detection.

steps.title: Inject samples and acquire data
steps.instruction: Inject each prepared 1 mL LC vial onto the column, record the chromatograms, and acquire arsenic species signals with the ICP‑MS/MS detector. Ensure that the run order includes the calibration standards, ICV, CCV, blanks, LOQ, and samples as defined in the QC schedule.

steps.title: Evaluate QC and accept data
steps.instruction: After each run, verify that the ICV, CCV, blanks, and LOQ meet their respective acceptance criteria. If any QC point falls outside its limits, discard the associated sample data, perform cleaning and maintenance of the instrument, and repeat the analysis of the affected samples.

steps.title: Perform method validation spikes
steps.instruction: In each analytical batch, spike one environmental sample with a mixture of As(III), As(V), DMA, and MMA to a final concentration of 10 µg L⁻¹ each. Analyze the unspiked parent sample and the spiked sample in duplicate and calculate the relative percent difference (RPD) between replicates. Additionally, run blind blanks consisting of ultrapure water preserved with 2.5 mM EDTA (n = 14) to monitor background.
